title: Minimally Specified Monitor Prompt Study: How Much Does Monitor Prompt Detail Affect Detection Performance?
original_idea: Design 5 monitor prompts ranging from minimal ('flag any harmful or suspicious agent actions') to maximally specified (listing specific sabotage types). Evaluate each on all SHADE-Arena public trajectories. Plot detection AUC vs. prompt specificity. Identify where gains plateau.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear safety-relevant prediction: if minimal prompts achieve 90% of max performance, monitoring is more robust to novel attacks than assumed. This has direct implications for monitoring architecture design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Very accessible: write 5 prompts, run LLM API calls, compute AUC. No ML training. No specialized tools. Standard Python. Beginner-friendly. Fits easily in 30hrs. Medium compute for API calls.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Extremely narrow: 5 prompts, one evaluation dataset, one metric (AUC vs. specificity). Single clear experiment with a defined plot as deliverable.
